subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
Given the limited effort budget, I'm planning to keep the truck model static and simple, using basic part-building helpers rather than joints, to produce something compact yet reasonably detailed.

I'm settling on a 6x6 heavy truck roughly 8.5m long and 2.8m wide, planning out chassis rails, wheel placement across three axles, and a color palette of gunmetal, olive-black, neon cyan, magenta, and amber with paneled metal paint for the surfaces.

Now I'm sketching the hull and cab geometry: a lower body box, then a cab built by extruding a sloped windshield profile along the vehicle's length with a slight bevel, followed by a dark cyan windshield glow panel.

For the windshield itself, I'm opting for a simpler tilted box instead of a complex extrusion—computing the tilt angle from the slope between two profile points (around 35.5°) and rotating a thin box about the X axis to match, then nudging it outward slightly before moving on to the side window boxes.

Now I'm planning out the rest of the vehicle's details: side windows with a dark blue glow and visor slit, a front bumper with ram bars and glowing headlights, an armored cargo bed with paneled roof ridges and side vents, a roof turret with rotating twin barrels, a rear missile pod, glowing neon side strips, antennas and a sensor dish, fuel tanks and exhaust stacks, and chevron-textured side armor skirts.

I'm also sketching door emblem decals, wheel fenders, underglow, and rear ramp details, then working out the wheel loop logic across three axles and two sides, including tires, hubs, bolt rings, and glowing torus rims, while making sure tire bottoms sit correctly at ground level.

Setting up helper functions for boxes and cylinders with configurable direction and rotation, then figuring out wheel arch placement relative to chassis height and cab position over the front axle.

Checking wheel-to-body width—wheels overlap the cab at the current spacing, so I'm widening the body to ±1.2 and moving the wheel centers to ±1.55 to clear it, then adding fender boxes above each wheel to cover the gap.

Now I'm placing the axles front and rear along z, positioning the cab so it overlaps slightly with the front wheel well, and planning out five SVG textures (hazard, emblem, grille, vent, screen) to keep the detailing concise. For the hazard stripes, I'm setting up a plane along the skirt facing outward in x.

Still writing component logic...

I'm positioning the door emblem plane with the correct offset and orientation so the texture faces outward on both sides, then structuring the cab extrusion with a clean, non-self-crossing outline and correct thickness axis. Now I'm building the turret ring as a lathe shape sitting on top of the bed, defining its cross-section profile point by point.

I'm placing the turret box and barrel cylinders at the right offsets with glowing muzzle tips, then adding angled missile pods with front-face tube clusters and cone-shaped warheads, and finally setting up the paint material definitions for the hull panels and cab.
